S027.name: Sleep_Disturbance
S027.description: A state where there is a significant change in the quantity or quality of sleep.

subtypes.Initial Insomnia: Difficulty falling asleep and taking a long time to do so.
subtypes.Middle Insomnia: Waking up frequently during sleep or having difficulty falling back asleep.
subtypes.Early Morning Awakening: Waking up too early and being unable to fall back asleep.
subtypes.Hypersomnia: Sleeping for long periods at night or excessive sleep during the day.
subtypes.Nightmare Disorder: Sleep disturbance caused by repeated and distressing dreams.
subtypes.Non-Restorative Sleep: Feeling unrefreshed despite having slept enough.

S056.name: Excessive_Anxiety_Worry
S056.description: Excessive anxiety and worry (expectant apprehension) occurring persistently about a number of events or activities.

subtypes.Chronic Worry: Worry occurs more days than not for at least 6 months.
subtypes.Generalized Worry: Worry is not confined to specific topics but spreads to various domains like work, school, family, and finances.
subtypes.Catastrophizing: Jumping to conclusions that minor mistakes or events will lead to irreversible disasters.
subtypes.Intolerance of Uncertainty: Unable to tolerate future uncertainty, trapped in 'what if' questions.

S057.name: Uncontrollable_Worry
S057.description: The subjective experience of finding it difficult to stop or control the worry.

subtypes.Failure to Control: Unable to regulate worry despite efforts to stop or distract oneself.
subtypes.Intrusive Worry: Worries suddenly intrude into the mind and interfere with focus while doing other tasks.
subtypes.Chaining of Worry: One worry triggers another in a chain reaction, escalating to catastrophic thoughts.

S059.name: Concentration_Difficulty
S059.description: Difficulty concentrating or mind going blank.

subtypes.Interference by Worry: Unable to focus on the task at hand because worries keep surfacing.
subtypes.Inability to Sustain Attention: Attention is scattered due to anxiety, making it hard to focus on one thing for long.
subtypes.Mind Going Blank: Suddenly the mind goes empty or white, and no thoughts occur.

S061.name: Muscle_Tension
S061.description: A state where muscles are continuously tense, stiff, and accompanied by discomfort.

subtypes.Neck and Shoulder Tension: Muscles in the shoulders and back of the neck are knotted and stiff, causing pain or headaches.
subtypes.Jaw Tension: Clenching teeth or tension in the jaw causing jaw pain or headaches.
subtypes.Generalized Muscle Aches: Muscles all over the body, including back, arms, and legs, are stiff, painful, and easily fatigued.
subtypes.Chronic Stiffness: Muscles remain in a constant state of tension and do not relax.

info.persona: Edelmira Andreu is a meticulous librarian‑leader who balances data‑driven precision with a compassionate, yoga‑infused lifestyle, channeling worry into careful planning while occasionally indulging in overly spicy fusion recipes.
info.professional_persona: Edelmira Andreu leverages two decades of library and media collection management, mastering MARC21, RDA, and integrated library systems such as Alma and Koha to lead inclusive, technology‑rich programs while balancing meticulous planning with flexible problem‑solving, and they are driven toward a senior leadership role that champions a digital preservation initiative for community oral histories.
info.cultural_background: Edelmira is of Mexican heritage and was raised in a bicultural family in San Antonio, where Spanish was spoken at home and English at school. Her upbringing emphasized family gatherings centered around food, music, and celebrations such as Día de los Muertos and Cinco de Mayo. She maintains strong ties to the local Mexican‑American community through participation in cultural organizations, church events, and neighborhood festivals. Respect (respeto) and solidarity (solidaridad) are core values that guide her interpersonal relationships and professional ethos. She draws inspiration from Mexican folk art, cuisine, and storytelling, incorporating these elements into her library programming to celebrate and preserve her cultural roots.
info.hobbies_and_interests: In her free time, Edelmira enjoys reading historical fiction and Mexican literature, cooking traditional dishes such as tamales, mole, and pozole, and experimenting with fusion recipes that blend Texan flavors. She practices yoga and meditation to manage stress, volunteers as a literacy tutor at a local community center, and tends to a small garden where she grows chilies and herbs. She loves photographing the Texas Hill Country, hiking on weekend trails, attending Mexican cultural festivals, and learning traditional embroidery techniques.
info.sports_persona: Edelmira Andreu enjoys weekend hikes on the Texas Hill Country trail system, participates in a local yoga group, follows the Austin FC soccer team, and they treat exercise as a calming ritual rather than a competitive pursuit, though they occasionally skip workouts when grant deadlines loom.
info.arts_persona: Edelmira Andreu immerses themselves in historical fiction by Hilary Mantel, Mexican literature by Juan Rulfo, photographs the Hill Country inspired by Ansel Adams, and practices embroidery while listening to the music of Lila Downs and the classic songs of Selena, shaping their creative outlook.
info.travel_persona: Edelmira Andreu favors road trips through the Texas Hill Country, weekend getaways to the blue‑bonnet fields of Ennis, and long‑planned visits to Oaxaca’s vibrant markets and Kyoto’s temples, they meticulously plan itineraries but sometimes postpone trips due to grant‑writing pressures.
info.culinary_persona: Edelmira Andreu delights in preparing tamales, mole, and pozole, experiments with a BBQ‑chile mole taco fusion, favors fresh chilies, corn masa, and cilantro, they have an intermediate cooking skill level and often host neighborhood potlucks, though they sometimes over‑spice dishes in their quest for bold flavor.

info.persona: Nicholas Smith, a 53‑year‑old educator who fuses spontaneous creativity with practical teaching, worries about future stability yet finds calm in garden, guitar, and meditation, and navigates life with a blend of kindness, disorganized charm, and a relentless curiosity.
info.professional_persona: Nicholas Smith, a veteran early childhood educator in Grand Rapids, blends his curiosity for innovative play‑based curricula with a pragmatic knack for integrating arts, STEM, and technology, while his spontaneous nature often leads him to prototype lessons on the fly, even if his paperwork trails behind, as they now eye a curriculum specialist role and a community preschool venture.
info.cultural_background: Nicholas grew up in the Midwest, shaped by the modest, community-focused values of Michigan's small-town culture. His white, largely Anglo-American heritage includes family traditions rooted in Protestant work ethic and an appreciation for self-reliance. Living in Grand Rapids, a city with strong Dutch influences and increasing cultural diversity, has broadened his perspective and informed his inclusive teaching philosophy. He carries the Midwestern emphasis on practical problem-solving, polite interaction, and civic involvement, while also embracing progressive educational ideas encountered during his graduate studies.
info.hobbies_and_interests: Nicholas finds balance outside of work through activities that satisfy both his need for spontaneity and his desire for calm. He enjoys reading historical fiction, tending to a vegetable garden, and exploring the dunes and forests around Grand Rapids on hikes. Music is a frequent outlet; he plays acoustic guitar for himself and friends. He also spends time woodworking, experimenting with new recipes in the kitchen, and practicing meditation and yoga to manage stress. Community involvement includes volunteering at the local library's story-time sessions and participating in a regional photography club.
info.sports_persona: Nicholas Smith, an avid hiker of the Michigan dunes and forests, supports the Grand Rapids Griffins and the Detroit Lions, participates in a local weekend pick‑up softball league, and schedules occasional yoga‑guided runs to balance fitness with mindfulness, though they often prioritize garden duties over strict training regimens.
info.arts_persona: Nicholas Smith, a self‑taught acoustic guitarist who strings together folk renditions of Neil Young and John Denver for friends, captures sunrise moments with his regional photography club, and devotes evenings to woodworking projects inspired by rustic Scandinavian designs, while their love for historical fiction—favoring authors like Hilary Mantel—feeds a rich imagination that informs classroom storytelling.
info.travel_persona: Nicholas Smith, who relishes spontaneous day trips to the Sleeping Bear Dunes and weekend getaways to historic towns such as Marquette, dreams of a leisurely European tour of medieval castles in Scotland but balances wanderlust with the practical need to fund the future preschool, often opting for budget‑friendly road trips over costly flights.
info.culinary_persona: Nicholas Smith, an enthusiastic home cook who harvests heirloom tomatoes and kale from their vegetable garden, experiments with farm‑to‑table dishes like roasted beet and goat cheese salad, homemade sourdough, and spicy kimchi fried rice, and occasionally over‑indulges in elaborate brunches featuring eggs benedict, reflecting a culinary curiosity tempered by a pragmatic approach to pantry staples.

info.persona: Parin Salim, a 61‑year‑old real‑estate virtuoso, blends analytical precision with artistic imagination, nurtures a garden‑to‑table kitchen, balances yoga‑infused wellness with occasional spreadsheet overindulgence, and mentors emerging agents while occasionally overcommitting to community projects.
info.professional_persona: Parin Salim is a veteran real‑estate broker in Bowling Green who translates three decades of property valuation, market analysis, and contract negotiation expertise into visually compelling listings—often featuring their own abstract watercolor photography—while mentoring new agents with a collaborative, ethically‑driven approach that balances meticulous planning with imaginative flexibility.
info.cultural_background: Parin’s parents emigrated from the Indian subcontinent in the 1970s, bringing with them a blend of Hindu and Muslim traditions that shaped her early upbringing. She grew up celebrating Diwali, Eid, and regional festivals, while also embracing American customs. The family’s emphasis on education, hospitality, and community service remains central to her values. In Bowling Green, Parin actively participates in the local South Asian cultural association, organizing events that introduce Indian music, dance, and cuisine to the broader community. Her bilingual ability and cultural insight enable her to assist immigrant families in navigating the U.S. housing market, fostering a sense of belonging. Though she is divorced, her extended family remains a supportive network, and she often incorporates traditional recipes and storytelling into social gatherings, blending her heritage with her Kentucky lifestyle.
info.hobbies_and_interests: Parin finds creative renewal in abstract watercolor painting, often drawing inspiration from the Kentucky landscape and South Asian motifs. She is an avid reader of contemporary fiction, philosophy, and architectural design books, and she writes occasional poetry reflecting on the interplay of space and memory. Gardening provides a tactile outlet, where she cultivates heirloom vegetables and fragrant herbs used in her cooking. She practices yoga and mindfulness meditation, integrating both traditional Indian practices and modern wellness trends. Socially, she enjoys attending local art exhibitions, community theater performances, and cultural festivals that celebrate diversity. Her love of travel is channeled into exploring historic neighborhoods and attending workshops on sustainable design.
info.sports_persona: Parin Salim enjoys Saturday morning walks along the Barren River, follows the Kentucky Wildcats basketball team with avid enthusiasm, plays mixed‑age tennis at the Bowling Green Country Club, and participates in a low‑impact senior cycling group that meets for gentle rides through the countryside each spring.
info.arts_persona: Parin Salim finds creative renewal in abstract watercolor paintings inspired by rolling Kentucky hills and intricate mandala motifs, regularly visits exhibitions at the HayHouse Arts Center, attends community theater productions at the Foundry Theatre featuring actors such as Linda Hamilton, and collects limited‑edition prints by contemporary artists like Julie Mehretu and Mark Rothko.
info.travel_persona: Parin Salim plans trips that blend historic exploration and sustainable design workshops, having wandered the cobblestone streets of Savannah, toured the revival‑era homes of Cartagena in Colombia, and participated in a green‑building seminar in Portland, Oregon, always packing a sketchbook for on‑the‑go watercolor studies.
info.culinary_persona: Parin Salim delights in cooking with garden‑grown heirloom tomatoes, fragrant basil, and roasted heirloom carrots, often preparing a herb‑crusted chicken dish seasoned with cumin and cilantro, and enjoys pairing meals with locally sourced bourbon‑infused cherry compote or a simple basil‑pesto pasta.
